content: The malignancy known as hairy cell leukemia was first referred to by this term in 1966 by Dr. R. Schrek and Dr. W. J. Donnelly. The condition initially described as leukemic reticuloendotheliosis was first identified in 1923 by Dr. O. Ewald, a German physician. Hairy cell leukemia was first recognized as a distinct clinicopathological entity in 1958, as reported by Dr. Bertha A. Bouroncle. The term hairy cell leukemia was officially introduced to describe this malignancy by Dr. R. Schrek and Dr. W. J. Donnelly in 1966. Further detailed insights into hairy cell leukemia were provided in 2008 by Fanta PT and Saven A in their publication in Cancer Treatment and Research (Volume 142, Pages 193–209).
